name: MONEY
description: Money is a two-player card game found in several Arab countries including Jordan, Syria, and Egypt. Players hold their cards in a face-down stack and must play the top card at each turn. The game combines elements of fishing games (capturing matching cards) with a unique 'money' system where picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are set aside and used to buy cards when a player runs out.

content.text: Money is a two-player card game found in several Arab countries including Jordan, Syria, and Egypt. Players hold their cards in a face-down stack and must play the top card at each turn. The game combines elements of fishing games (capturing matching cards) with a unique 'money' system where picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are set aside and used to buy cards when a player runs out.

Money is played in several Arab countries. The name refers to the picture cards which serve as currency in the game. It shares mechanics with children's games like Beggar My Neighbour and Snap, but adds the sophisticated buying mechanic.

Two players. The game is normally played with a standard 52-card pack; some variants add two Jokers. Before dealing, all picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are removed. Each player receives two Kings, two Queens, and two Jacks as their starting money, stored face up in a money area or bank. The remaining 40 numeral cards (Aces count as 1s) are shuffled and dealt equally, 20 cards each, as face-down stacks that players must not look at or reorder.
Standard 52-card pack. Optional: 2 Jokers can be added. Suits are irrelevant.
Standard deck, space for 'money area' (bank) and 'floor' (play pile).
